items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips | TechCrunch
items.summary:
The chip launch comes as hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon, and even AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are working on their own lines of AI-specific semiconductors and accompanying software in order to reduce their reliance on the dominance of Nvidia.

The news also comes at a particularly vulnerable moment for Nvidia, whose CEO Jensen Huang over the weekend admitted to having an affair with someone alleged to be a Chinese spy. [...] The chip also has a custom inferencing network that lets it run reasoning alongside training, so it can be used to distill and train small models on the fly. That ability, according to Google, could prove useful for cases where a company might want to train a model on its proprietary data without having to move the data between devices. [...] Google is notching up its chipmaking game as the company seeks to reduce its dependence on chips made by other companies for its cloud computing business. Google on Monday unveiled two new variants of its tensor processing units (TPUs), in-house developed chips meant for AI workloads, that broaden its chip portfolio to additional use cases: confidential inference and more memory capacity for large workloads.

items.title: Hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp ứng dụng công nghệ, nâng cao sức cạnh tranh
items.summary: Tiến sĩ Chu Thúc Đạt, Phó Cục trưởng Cục Đổi mới sáng tạo (Bộ Khoa học và Công nghệ) cho biết, trong bối cảnh cạnh tranh ngày càng gay gắt, năng lực công nghệ có vai trò quan trọng, trực tiếp ảnh hưởng đến năng suất, chất lượng sản phẩm, hiệu quả sử dụng nguyên liệu và khả năng tham gia chuỗi giá trị của doanh nghiệp ngành chế biến, chế tạo. Trên cơ sở Chương trình phối hợp giai đoạn 2026 - 2030 với định hướng thúc đẩy khoa học, công nghệ và đổi mới sáng tạo gắn với các chuỗi giá trị ngành hàng [...] Chia sẻ về thực tiễn ứng dụng công nghệ vào sản xuất, Phó Giám đốc Công ty Trách nhiệm hữu hạn Sản xuất thương mại Phước Thành IV  Huỳnh Hồng Thắm cho biết, công ty đang đề xuất tiếp cận công nghệ chế biến khoai lang tím nhằm đa dạng hóa đầu ra, gắn sản phẩm chế biến với nhu cầu thị trường và người tiêu dùng. Với nền tảng công nghệ sẵn có trong lĩnh vực chế biến, kinh doanh gạo, đóng gói bao bì, cùng kinh nghiệm cải tiến quy trình sản xuất, công ty có điều kiện tiếp nhận, ứng dụng công nghệ mới [...] giá trị ngành hàng chủ lực, hội thảo là dịp để cụ thể hóa các nội dung phối hợp thông qua việc xác định nhu cầu công nghệ của doanh nghiệp, kết nối với các giải pháp phù hợp và huy động nguồn lực hỗ trợ triển khai vào thực tiễn sản xuất.

items.title: Cổ phiếu công nghệ Mỹ biến động trước lo ngại về quy định AI | NHK WORLD-JAPAN News
items.summary:
Một số chuyên gia cho rằng các công ty trung tm dữ liệu mới nổi có thể gặp khó khăn về vốn nếu các quy định chặt chẽ hơn làm chậm tiến độ các dự án xy dựng mới. Các công ty này đã dựa vào khoản vay để mở rộng kinh doanh.  
   
Nguồn tin thị trường cho biết điều đó có nghĩa là cổ phiếu công nghệ có thể vẫn bất ổn trong thời gian trước mắt. [...] Chiến thắng áp đảo của đảng Dn chủ trong cuộc bầu cử giữa kỳ của Mỹ đã làm dấy lên lo ngại về triển vọng của ngành trí tuệ nhn tạo và bán dẫn. Điều này khiến cổ phiếu công nghệ cao của Mỹ biến động.  
   
Đảng Dn chủ đã giành lại quyền kiểm soát cả hai viện Quốc hội trong cuộc bầu cử tuần trước. Các ứng viên đảng Dn chủ cũng chiến thắng trong các cuộc bầu cử thống đốc ở nhiều bang, trong đó có Texas, nơi có nhiều trung tm dữ liệu. [...] Một số nhà đầu tư lo ngại những chiến thắng này có thể dẫn đến việc siết chặt quy định đối với AI và các trung tm dữ liệu.  
   
Mối lo này đã gy ra làn sóng bán tháo cổ phiếu bán dẫn và các cổ phiếu khác liên quan đến AI. Hôm thứ Năm, chỉ số Nasdaq gồm nhiều cổ phiếu công nghệ ở New York giảm hơn 5%. Cổ phiếu công nghệ đã phần nào khôi phục vào ngày hôm sau nhưng các nhà đầu tư vẫn thận trọng.

items.summary: Theo hướng dẫn, các giải pháp được xem xét công nhận là sáng kiến bao gồm: giải pháp kỹ thuật, giải pháp quản lý, giải pháp tác nghiệp và giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật. Trong đó, giải pháp kỹ thuật có thể là sản phẩm, vật liệu, giống cy trồng, vật nuôi hoặc quy trình công nghệ; giải pháp quản lý là phương pháp tổ chức, điều hành công việc; giải pháp tác nghiệp là các phương pháp thực hiện nghiệp vụ chuyên môn; còn giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật là việc áp dụng các giải pháp kỹ thuật [...] Đối với các đề tài khoa học, đề án khoa học và công trình khoa học – công nghệ, việc xét nghiệm thu thực hiện theo quy định của pháp luật về khoa học và công nghệ. Các đề tài chỉ được xem xét công nhận hiệu quả áp dụng và phạm vi ảnh hưởng khi đã được nghiệm thu đạt yêu cầu trở lên. [...] giải pháp kỹ thuật đã có vào thực tiễn.

items.title: Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now les
items.summary:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

[...] TPU 8tx, designed with AMD, is based on the TPU 8t chip, and is geared specifically for confidentially training and running AI models, Google said in a blog post. items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. [...] Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet.

items.title: OpenAI’s Plan to Stop AI Data Centres Overloading the Grid | Energy Digital
items.summary:
A vocal section of the American electorate were seeking assurances that AI companies will not overload power grids, while many candidates ran on a ticket of holding hyperscalers to account.

Before a single vote was counted, though, OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, had unveiled its ‘Grid Protectors Program’ – an initiative that will see its future computing campuses ease pressure on the grid. [...] “Data centres are paying more so families and small businesses can pay less, and our goal with every contract we sign under this framework is to deliver value for them,” she says

At OpenAI, the bigger picture is always in focus.

“With US data centre capacity projected to exceed 100 gigawatts by 2030⁠, we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to strengthen the electric grid by building campuses that can adjust their power use when communities need it most,” the company says. [...] OpenAI is working to ensure its data centres can actually benefit grids, rather than overloading them. Credit: Anna Moneymaker/Getty

## What is OpenAI’s Grid Protectors Program?

The programme, which was announced on 2 November, commits the company to working with utilities, regulators and policymakers on arrangements for cutting the power use of its data centres at times of need.

items.title: OpenAI wants to be Google - Fast Company
items.summary:
OpenAI needs to build analytics that show advertisers the consumer intent based on their prompts. I want to know which categories of intent my impressions ran against. I want to know whether those people were exploring, comparing, or ready to act, and which needs and product criteria drove that engagement. I want to know which kinds of sweater prompts turned into business and, just as important, which didn’t. Google’s advertisers have had some version of that map for two decades. It’s why [...] |

That comparison is where every sweater brand wants to be standing, and OpenAI has started selling the spot. Advertisers can buy on a CPM or CPC basis through OpenAI’s beta self-service Ads Manager, measure conversions with a pixel and Conversions API, and access campaign-level performance reporting. OpenAI is also testing Sponsored Agents, which let a user start a separate conversation with an advertiser after clicking an ad.

So the plumbing exists.

## A SEARCH-CALIBER AD PLATFORM [...] OpenAI already has the hard part down, the thing Google spent years teaching people to do. People are telling ChatGPT their goals, problems, preferences, objections, and purchase criteria in their own words. What it hasn’t built is the advertiser’s map of all that intent.

items.title: SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI: 3 giant IPOs and only 1 has sold shares
items.summary:
OpenAI has little reason to hurry while private investors keep funding it, and it has closed $11 billion in new money. The company has also given its own reason to wait. "We have not decided on timing yet; it may be a while because there are things we want to do that are likely easier as a private company," OpenAI said in a statement, as reportedby CNBC. Public buyers would also have to judge a trillion-dollar price without some basic facts about the business. Most of OpenAI's sales come from [...] The private valuation has climbed fast, and the figure public buyers will pay is still unsettled. Private investors valued OpenAI at $852 billion in late March, according to CNBC. Sam Altman, OpenAI's chief executive, is aiming for a $1 trillion valuation in the listing, according to Bloomberg reporting carried by The Next Web. That target is lower than what private investors last paid, which means the debut may not be priced at the private peak. Whether public buyers match the latest round or [...] The verdict on Anthropic will come only after trading begins, when buyers without a business stake decide whether $78 a share was worth paying.

## OpenAI

Illustration: Quartz

OpenAI has not yet sold a single share to the public, but private investors already value it at $1.25 trillion, according to Reuters. That valuation puts its planned listing among the largest stock market debuts. Nobody yet knows how much stock OpenAI will sell or when, so the size of its debut remains unknown.
